## Assumptions — 32 rows (P1.1 13, P1.2 8, P1.3 6, P1.4 5)

| # | Source | Assumption | How to verify | Impact if false |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | P1.1 #1 | `[DEFAULT-1]` `instrument_id` is per listing venue, not per issuer | Owner ratification; or the first dual-listed India name at the ADR-11 activation gate | Cross-venue aggregation needs an `issuer_id` rollup — a reporting join, not a migration, since `issuer_id` already exists |
| A2 | P1.1 #2 | `[DEFAULT-2]` `Price` at 6 dp is sufficient | Inspect the widest observed decimal in a month of `Trade` prints during P2.1 | If a vendor emits >6 dp, prices truncate silently; the check is one query and belongs in P2.2's quality gate |
| A3 | P1.1 #3 | `[DEFAULT-3]` Fractional shares are unreachable in v1 | Alpaca order-type documentation for fractional; re-read at P3.1 | If fractional works with limit orders, `qty_increment` becomes a per-instrument value and sizing gains resolution at small NAV. No schema change — the field already exists |
| A4 | P1.1 #4 | `[DEFAULT-4]` Largest-remainder allocation with ascending-index tie-break | Assert `sum(allocate(w)) == total` over a property-based test in P5.4 | A different tie-break changes cent placement; deterministic replay would diverge between two implementations |
| A5 | P1.1 #5 | `[DEFAULT-5]` Naive datetimes are rejected, not coerced | Owner ratification | Ingest adapters for a vendor that emits naive timestamps need an explicit tz declaration — which is the correct outcome |
| A6 | P1.1 #6 | `[DEFAULT-6]` India has no wash-sale rule, so the field must be `NULL` for `IN` | A qualified Indian tax professional (P0.1 open item Q8) | If India has an analogous rule, the validator inverts and the India tax export needs the field |
| A7 | P1.1 #7 | `[DEFAULT-7]` `RegimeLabel` is the four `[RS §13]` labels plus `UNKNOWN` | P2.6 design | Adding a member is additive and cheap; the closed enum is what matters, not the exact membership |
| A8 | P1.1 #8 | `[DEFAULT-8]` `[CONST-2]` is enforced structurally at the `Decision` constructor | Red-team template X4 — attempt to construct a `Decision` from a `Thesis` | If a bypass exists, `[CONST-1]` is decorative. This is the single highest-value test in the suite |
| A9 | P1.1 #9 | `[DEFAULT-9]` P1.1 owns the audit envelope, P1.4 the catalogue | P1.4 reconciles at its own freeze | If P1.4 wants the envelope too, the two must merge — a rename, not a redesign |
| A10 | P1.1 #10 | `[DEFAULT-10]` `UNKNOWN` is a persisted order state | P3.1 broker adapter design | Without it, an ambiguous broker response becomes a retry and then a duplicate order |
| A11 | P1.1 #11 | US and India equity settlement are both T+1 | Broker settlement documentation; NSE settlement calendar | `settlement_date` is computed by the calendar loader from a configured cycle, so a different cycle is a config change. But `settled_cash` sizing would be wrong in the interim — this is the highest-impact unverified assumption in this spec |
| A12 | P1.1 #12 | A merger preserves the tax holding period and cost basis on a share-for-share exchange | A qualified tax professional, both jurisdictions | Lot `opened_on` would reset on conversion, changing STCG/LTCG classification in India and wash-sale windows in the US |
| A13 | P1.1 #13 | FIFO is the correct cost-basis method | A qualified tax professional | `CostBasisMethod` is already an enum with `LIFO` and `AVERAGE`, so the change is a config value plus a re-run of the lot consumer |
| A14 | P1.2 #1 | `[DEFAULT-S1]` `SECURITY DEFINER` as-of functions cover every legitimate backtest read | Review against P5.1's queries at its freeze | A missing function blocks a backtest — loud and safe, which is the intended direction of failure |
| A15 | P1.2 #2 | `[DEFAULT-S4]` 6 dp is enough price precision through the November 2027 regime | P1.1 Q-P1.1-6: `max(scale(price))` over a month of prints | Truncation on a higher-precision vendor. Detected by the P2.2 quality gate |
| A16 | P1.2 #3 | 15× / 4× compression ratios | RULE-B2: day 45, ≥3 chunks, live-written only (query Q-14) | At 8× overall, year-10 compressed is ~19 GB and on-VM ~62 GB — still 4× headroom on 250 GB |
| A17 | P1.2 #4 | ~1,000 B mean `audit_log` row | Measurement-by-design **Q15**, after 20 live sessions, via `cagg_audit_events_daily` | P0.3 §9.4 already stress-tests to 10×: at 150,000 events/session the 250 GB volume needs resizing. Below 5× it holds |
| A18 | P1.2 #5 | ~8 KB mean `llm_call` row | Measurement-by-design **Q14**, first 50 live gate calls | 4× would be 300 MB compressed — still immaterial |
| A19 | P1.2 #6 | ~200 news items/day with revision factor `rf` unmeasured | Count revision rows after 3 months of forward collection | At `rf = 3`, +250 MB compressed. P0.3 already declares this immaterial against 4.7× headroom |
| A20 | P1.2 #7 | `pgbackrest` is the archive tool | P6.4 deployment | Any tool with WAL push and PITR substitutes; `archive_command` is one line |
| A21 | P1.2 #8 | An off-VM WAL receiver is reachable with low enough latency for the 5 s intraday budget | **Q-P1.2-2** — measure commit latency to the chosen target before go-live | If it exceeds the budget, the intraday exit path moves to `local` durability with a stated, audited RPO > 0 for exits only — a real reduction in ADR-10's guarantee that must be taken as a decision, not absorbed |
| A22 | P1.3 #1 | `[DEFAULT-C4]` `cryptography` is acceptable despite `[CONST]`'s dependency rule | Owner ratification of the dependency | Fall back to HMAC and abandon per-approver attribution — i.e. abandon the two-person rule as a *provable* control |
| A23 | P1.3 #2 | `[DEFAULT-C7]` Two approvers is the right number | Owner decision | If 1 is correct, `min_approvals_to_loosen` drops to 1 and the `Governance` validator relaxes. Note the validator currently *forbids* 1, so this is a deliberate one-way door |
| A24 | P1.3 #3 | India universe thresholds (`min_price_inr`, ranks) | ADR-11's India activation gate; NSE listing statistics | India is unfunded, so nothing live depends on it. Wrong values would mis-size the India universe on the day the gate opens — **Q-P1.3-2** |
| A25 | P1.3 #4 | `MAX_MODIFY_PASSES = 4` is enough | P2.9 integration; assert the pass count never exceeds 2 in practice | If a future rule pair oscillates, the verdict is DENY — fail-closed, but a silently un-tradeable name. Instrument the pass count |
| A26 | P1.3 #5 | Ed25519 public key is retrievable from Vault at boot | P6.2 | If Vault is unreachable at boot the process does not start — correct, and consistent with ADR-09 row 11's fail-closed halt |
| A27 | P1.3 #6 | `assumed_round_trip_bps` 25 US / 90 IN | P5.3, after ≥200 **live** fills (rule N11 excludes paper) | `EDGE-001` gates on it. Too low → trades that do not clear cost; too high → no trades. Measurement-by-design **Q13** |
| A28 | P1.4 #1 | 18,538 events/s holds at 10M rows | Re-benchmark against 10M rows loaded from TimescaleDB during P6.4 | The real cost adds I/O — the projection covers CPU only. If disk-bound, verification becomes a streaming job rather than a batch one. **Recorded as Q-P1.4-3** |
| A29 | P1.4 #2 | `[DEFAULT-A8]` No natural-person data enters the log | Review at P6.3 | If the ownership model changes, §8.2 is void, GDPR/DPDP erasure conflicts head-on with an immutable log, and that conflict is an ADR-09 row 12 amendment |
| A30 | P1.4 #3 | Off-VM anchor storage is write-once with distinct credentials | P6.2/P6.4 | An anchor store the database's credentials can rewrite provides **no** additional guarantee — it would be security theatre, and worse than none because it would be believed |
| A31 | P1.4 #4 | One anchor per session bounds the blast radius acceptably | Q-P1.4-2 — check whether SEBI or SEC name one | A required cadence tightens the parameter; the mechanism is unchanged |
| A32 | P1.4 #5 | ~1 KB mean event, 15,000/session | Measurement-by-design **Q15**, via `cagg_audit_events_daily` after 20 live sessions | P0.3 §9.4 stress-tests to 10×; at 150,000/session the 250 GB volume needs resizing |
